outline.description: This chapter establishes the factual foundation of *Cohen v. Consilio*, detailing the employment relationship, the specific policy change regarding overtime compensation, and the initial filing of the lawsuit. It outlines the unique procedural history where the defendant voluntarily paid all claimed back wages and liquidated damages prior to summary judgment, leaving only statutory penalties and injunctive relief in dispute.
subtopics: Employment Context: Hourly Licensed Attorney Document Reviewers at Consilio
The Policy Change: Elimination of Overtime Premium Pay in 2019
Claims Asserted: Violations of MPWA, MFLSA, and MWTA
Voluntary Remediation: Payment of Back Wages and Liquidated Damages Prior to Summary Judgment
Stipulations Between Parties Regarding Unpaid Penalties

outline.chapter_title: Standard of Review and Jurisdictional Thresholds
outline.description: Before analyzing the merits of the specific statutory claims, this chapter defines the appellate standard applied to summary judgment decisions in the Eighth Circuit. It introduces critical threshold doctrines relevant to this case, specifically focusing on Article III standing, mootness in the context of voluntary cessation of unlawful conduct, and the requirement that a plaintiff maintain a personal stake in every form of relief sought throughout litigation.
subtopics: De Novo Review Standard for Summary Judgment Grants
Viewing Evidence in Light Most Favorable to Non-Moving Party
Article III Standing Requirements for Civil Penalty Claims
The Doctrine of Mootness: Voluntary Cessation vs. Absolute Clarity of Non-Recurance
Requirement for Continuing Personal Interest Throughout Litigation

outline.chapter_title: Statutory Interpretation Under the Minnesota Payment of Wages Act (MPWA)
outline.description: This chapter analyzes why the court affirmed summary judgment against Cohen's claim for 'average daily wage penalties' under the MPWA. It details the court's textualist approach to statutory construction, contrasting § 181.101 with other sections of Minnesota law where private rights to penalties were explicitly granted by the legislature.
subtopics: Textual Analysis of Minn. Stat. Ann. § 181.171 and § 181.101(a)
Exclusive Authority: The Role of the Commissioner Versus Private Employees
'Know How' Canon: Legislative Intent Derived from Contrasting Statutory Schemes (§§ 181.13/181.14)
Application to Facts: Why Cohen Cannot Seek Average Daily Wage Penalties Privately

outline.chapter_title: Jurisdictional Uncertainty Under the Minnesota Fair Labor Standards Act (MFLSA)
outline.description: This section addresses the pivotal issue regarding Cohen's claim for MFLSA statutory penalties. Although Cohen was made whole financially regarding back wages, he sought penalties payable to the state Commissioner. This chapter explores why this created a potential mootness problem requiring remand rather than immediate dismissal or affirmation.
outline.subtopics: ["Distinction Between Employee Compensation (Overtime/Damages) and State Penalties", "Analysis of Potential Mootness Following Full Payment", "Evaluating Whether Wrongful Conduct Could Reasonably Be Expected to Recur", "Vacatur and Remand Order for District Court Determination on Jurisdiction"]
